name: James
overview: James was a male figure known primarily as the father of Judas (Thaddaeus), as recorded in Luke 6:16. There is no information about his tribe or additional notes. His identity is grounded in this familial connection within the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name James means 'follower, replacer, one who follows at the heel,' reflecting its Hebrew or Greek origins. This name appears as a proper name in Luke 6:16 and is not indicated to be given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: James is identified as the father of Thaddaeus (also known as Judas), according to Luke 6:16. Beyond this, Scripture does not record further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: James holds significance as the father of one of Jesus' apostles, Thaddaeus, linking him to the foundational circle of Christ's followers. While details about James himself are limited, his connection to an apostle situates him within the early church's narrative. His familial role underscores the importance of individual faith and commitment within families connected to Jesus' ministry.
